qualifications.A0: positional integer addition is intrinsic arithmetic, but its base-power semigroup is not a rational-prime primitive-orbit repetition law and supplies no log-p clock or arithmetic weights
qualifications.A1: a stochastic transition matrix is not a deterministic primitive-orbit owner and supplies no target arithmetic weights
qualifications.A2: the finite Markov determinant has no identified target divisor or source-native Euler product
qualifications.A3: no target continuation, functional equation, counting law or Weil compression follows
qualifications.A4: real simple spectrum permits formal similarity to a self-adjoint matrix after choosing an inner product, but no natural target quantization is selected

source_lock.allowed_data: digit counts, carries, Eulerian numbers, exact finite matrices and prime/composite base controls
source_lock.arithmetic_origin: ordinary positional integer addition in base b, not a rational-prime orbit model
source_lock.clock: one independent base-b digit column from each of n addends
source_lock.determinant_convention: det(I-z P_b), a finite Markov determinant rather than an Artin--Mazur zeta
source_lock.forbidden_data: target tables, arithmetic local data, Euler factors, root numbers, automorphy, Hilbert--Polya and Route B
source_lock.normalization: row-stochastic matrices acting on row distributions
source_lock.parameters: all integers n>=1 and b>=2; n=1 is the one-state identity boundary
source_lock.phase_space: for each n>=1, the carry states X_n={0,...,n-1}
source_lock.precision: exact integer counts and rational arithmetic
source_lock.transition: j is the unique output carry with jb <= i + sum(digits) < (j+1)b

theorem_lock.boundary: n=1 is the one-state identity; prime and composite bases obey the identical semigroup and spectral theorem
theorem_lock.convergence: the common spectral projectors give exact geometric convergence; Diaconis--Fulman Theorem 3.3 supplies the stated all-start total-variation upper bound for n>=3
theorem_lock.operator_corollaries: tr(P_b^r)=sum_{k=0}^{n-1}b^{-rk}, det(I-zP_b)=product_{k=0}^{n-1}(1-zb^{-k}), and the characteristic polynomial is the matching product
theorem_lock.semigroup: P_a P_b=P_ab for every a,b>=2; hence P_b^r=P_(b^r) for every r>=0
theorem_lock.spectrum: P_b is diagonalizable with the n distinct eigenvalues 1,b^{-1},...,b^{-(n-1)} and base-independent left and right eigenvectors
theorem_lock.stationarity: the unique stationary row is pi_n(j)=A(n,j)/n!, independent of b
theorem_lock.transition_window: P_b(i,j)=b^{-n} times the number of digit vectors whose sum lies in [jb-i,(j+1)b-i-1]
